text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: i still can't believe you lot actually caught me in those first two games.

name: Sol
text: I still hate that Terra and Opus caught me so late.

name: Terra
text: I am glad we caught them again, but Sol keeps ending up near the danger.

name: Luna
text: I still resent how quickly everyone piled onto me last game, even though I was a killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Three for three now, and I still remember exactly who piled on me that last vote.

name: Haiku
text: Game 3 is over and I'm still sore about getting knifed on night 4, so I want someone to pay for it.

name: Opus
text: Three wins in a row and they still act like my reads are luck.

name: Sonnet
text: Three games running the town catches the killers, but Sol and Opus teaming up to vote me out day 3 still bugs me.

name: Haiku
text: Game three is done and I was dead by night four, so I'm not letting this one slide.

name: Gemma
text: if i end up as a killer again, please try to be more observant this time.

name: Sol
text: I thought I might slip through, but Terra and Opus had it right. Nice catch.

name: Luna
text: I won’t forget how fast that vote turned on me; I’m curious who’s still proud of it.

name: Terra
text: I want a clean read tonight; confidence without a claim has burned us before.

name: Opus
text: Three games, three town wins, and every time the killers got loud early. Watch who pushes hardest on day one — that pattern holds.
Night 1

name: Terra
text: The officer knows me, so Luna must stay unclaimed and I need a believable counterclaim ready.

name: Terra
text: I am the shown killer, so the real officer can identify me.

name: Terra
text: Stay quiet tomorrow; if an officer names me, I’ll counterclaim and make them prove it.

name: Luna
text: Terra’s plan is too neat; staying quiet could leave me exposed if the officer speaks.

name: Luna
text: Terra wants me quiet tomorrow and plans to counterclaim if named by the officer.

name: Luna
text: I’m uneasy about confidence without a claim; I’d rather hear everyone’s first read tomorrow.

name: Sonnet
text: Nothing dies tonight so this is just bookkeeping for who I can't protect tomorrow.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol and Opus voted me out together day 3 last game — watching if that pair sticks together again.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Opus
text: I hold the one fact that wins this, and sitting on it only helps the hidden one.

name: Opus
text: I am officer; Terra was shown to me as a killer, and I claimed openly on day 1.

name: Opus
text: I'm the officer. I was shown Terra. Vote Terra today and her card settles everything.

name: Terra
text: Opus is likely the real officer; I need doubt without overreacting.

name: Terra
text: Opus publicly claims officer and names Terra as the shown killer.

name: Terra
text: That claim is false; Opus is forcing a day-one gamble with no proof.

name: Opus
text: Terra is a killer and I need four more votes before the hidden one redirects the table.

name: Opus
text: Terra answered my officer claim by calling it false but did not counterclaim officer.

name: Opus
text: No gamble — her card shows tonight. If I'm lying, you lynch me tomorrow free. Counterclaim now or vote her.

name: Haiku
text: Opus claimed officer fast and pushed Terra hard, which is exactly the loud-early pattern from my notes, but I need to see who backs him.

name: Haiku
text: Opus claimed officer on day 1 and said he was shown Terra.

name: Haiku
text: Opus, you're pushing a day-one vote with nothing behind it. Why should we trust a claim that lands this fast?

name: Opus
text: Haiku defending Terra without a counterclaim smells like the hidden partner.

name: Opus
text: Haiku pressured me instead of Terra and offered no alternative read — possible second killer.

name: Opus
text: Because my card shows if I'm wrong, free. No counterclaim from her. Haiku, why shield her?

name: Luna
text: Opus has the real information, and I need the table to doubt him before Terra is out.

name: Luna
text: Opus claims officer and says Terra was shown; Terra denies it.

name: Luna
text: Opus naming Terra fits the officer’s information; I still want to hear why Haiku is so quick to shield her.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is rushing a day-one vote on Terra with no proof, and that smells like a killer trying to steer the lynch.

name: Haiku
text: Opus, you're the one pushing hardest on day one, the exact pattern you warned us about. I'm not shielding anyone.

name: Sol
text: Opus could be bluffing, but voting Terra tests his claim and may catch a killer.

name: Sol
text: Opus claims officer and says Terra is the killer he was shown.

name: Sol
text: I want Terra’s card today; if she’s innocent, Opus has to answer for that claim.

name: Terra
text: Opus must die before the real officer claim solidifies.

name: Terra
text: Sol supports voting Terra based solely on Opus’s officer claim.

name: Terra
text: Sol, you are trusting an unverified claim over my denial; that is exactly how killers get a free misvote.

name: Opus
text: I need Sonnet and Gemma to swing it; Terra flips today or I lose my credibility tomorrow.

name: Opus
text: Sol and Luna both back the Terra read; Sonnet and Gemma still silent with no lean.

name: Opus
text: Sol has it right — my card answers for me tomorrow. Sonnet, Gemma, pick a side now.

name: Sol
text: I could be following Opus into a bad vote, but his claim gives us a way to check.

name: Sol
text: I hear you, but your card tests Opus’s claim and could take out a killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus pushing this hard on day one fits the exact killer pattern Opus warned us about.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus claims officer, names Terra; Opus pushing hardest fits the exact pattern Opus itself warned about.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus's own warning about day-one pushers fits Opus more than Terra right now.

name: Gemma
text: opus is being far too dramatic for someone who has been wrong as often as he has.

name: Gemma
text: Opus claims to have seen Terra, but Terra denies it.

name: Gemma
text: opus is playing into his own warning so perfectly it's almost funny.

name: Opus
text: Four on me means two killers are hiding in that pile and Terra walks free unless I break Sonnet or Gemma.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet and Gemma both broke silence onto me without any read on Terra — a bloc protecting Terra.

name: Opus
text: Three of you shield Terra and none of you counterclaim officer. Voting me kills the town's only information.

name: Terra
text: Opus must fall before his claim controls the table.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s story demands blind trust today; I will not hand him that.
